'''E. Glenadine Gibb''' was a mathematics education researcher who studied children's thinking about arithmetic operations.<ref>{{Cite book |title=A history of school mathematics |date=2003 |publisher=National Council of Teachers of Mathematics |isbn=978-0-87353-471-0 |editor-last=Stanic |editor-first=George M. A. |location=Reston, VA |pages=1647 |chapter=Chapter 36: The U.S. Mathematics Education Research Community |editor-last2=Kilpatrick |editor-first2=Jeremy}}</ref> She served as the president of [[National Council of Teachers of Mathematics]] (NCTM) from 1974 to 1976.<ref name=gibb1 />

Gibb was the first faculty member of the [[University of Texas]] Department of Curriculum and Instruction to be appointed to an endowed professorship, the Catherine Mae Parker Centennial Professorship in Education.<ref name="gibb1">{{Cite web |last=Association |first=Texas State Historical |title=E. Glenadine Gibb: Pioneer in Mathematics Education |url=https://www.tshaonline.org/handbook/entries/gibb-elizabeth-glenadine |access-date=2026-01-16 |website=Texas State Historical Association |language=en}}</ref>
